questions.question: What must feel materially better when this robustness work is complete?
questions.assumed: A new user can launch Forge3D, see a truthful connection state, work without colliding controls, exchange scene files reliably, and obtain designs that agents verify rather than merely claim are finished.

questions.question: Who is the primary user for these improvements?
questions.assumed: A local desktop user collaborating with one MCP agent while watching and correcting a live Blender scene.

questions.question: Which reported areas are required in this pass?
questions.assumed: Connection startup, responsive UI containment, save/open/import/export reliability, agent guidance and tool focus, accuracy evaluation, and a whole-project verification gate.

questions.question: What remains out of scope?
questions.assumed: Cloud accounts, collaborative multi-writer editing, new 3D file formats, and replacing Blender's modelling engine.

questions.question: How should top-bar commands behave when horizontal space is tight?
questions.assumed: Use one shared layout with no independent fixed offsets; retain primary status/actions and collapse secondary labels or actions before 529px without overlap.

questions.question: Where should agent connection state live?
questions.assumed: A compact status/action in the shared top bar, with details and repair actions in an accessible dialog.

questions.question: What is the minimum supported desktop viewport?
questions.assumed: 529 CSS pixels, preserving the existing rendered regression width and requiring zero command or panel collisions there and above.

questions.question: How should chat, selected-object editing, and logs share the sidebar?
questions.assumed: Chat receives flexible space; object editing and logs are bounded, collapsible sections that never draw over one another.

questions.question: What happens when selected-object controls are taller than their allocated panel?
questions.assumed: The inspector scrolls internally with its actions kept reachable; it does not expand across chat or logs.

questions.question: Which texture controls should be visible immediately?
questions.assumed: Preset and essential material/map state remain visible; mapping transforms and advanced tuning are grouped and collapsible, with styles matching the actual markup.

questions.question: What should automatic connection do at application startup?
questions.assumed: Reconnect the live viewer socket, immediately detect supported MCP clients, and show ready, restart-required, action-required, or unavailable without waiting for a click.

questions.question: May startup silently rewrite external AI-client configuration files?
questions.assumed: No. External config writes require an explicit Configure action; already-correct configurations are recognized automatically and never rewritten.

questions.question: What should users see after a client configuration is changed?
questions.assumed: A truthful restart-required state naming the affected client, plus refresh and retry actions; never claim a client is live merely because its file was written.

questions.question: What should happen when opening or importing while an agent run is active?
questions.assumed: Explain that the scene will change, pause safely before mutation, serialize the operation, and remain paused afterward so the user can inspect the result.

questions.question: What should export include by default?
questions.assumed: The whole current scene, with explicit selection-only scope when the UI offers it; unsupported formats fail clearly without presenting a partial result as success.

questions.question: Which file journeys require production guarantees?
questions.assumed: Native .forge3d save/open and GLB export/import receive real-Blender round-trip coverage; every advertised format keeps unit-level validation.

questions.question: How should long-running file work behave?
questions.assumed: Return a job immediately, report progress/errors in the existing UI, but marshal every Blender mutation onto its owning thread and serialize it with agent writes.

questions.question: What proves the file system works rather than merely exposing menu labels?
questions.assumed: API lifecycle tests, browser-state tests, and a small real-Blender save/open plus GLB export/import round trip all pass and assert downloadable non-empty artifacts.

questions.question: Should agents continue seeing all 52 tools in every design phase?
questions.assumed: No. List orientation, inspection, promotion, and only mutation tools legal in the current phase; keep raw execution out of the default MCP catalogue while preserving explicit opt-in compatibility.

questions.question: What workflow should every connected agent be instructed to follow?
questions.assumed: Orient with get_phase, prefer semantic operations, inspect ActionReport problems and assumptions, measure important dimensions, correct failures, and promote only after acceptance passes.

questions.question: What should get_phase provide before mutation begins?
questions.assumed: Current phase, callable focused catalogue, failed acceptance checks, user annotations/focus, and a concise recommended next-action sequence.

questions.question: How should attention to detail be evaluated?
questions.assumed: Representative tasks score orientation, semantic tool choice, dimension verification, defect repair, phase completion, and export rather than relying on prompt wording or tool counts alone.

questions.question: How should compatibility be handled for clients that expect the old catalogue?
questions.assumed: Tool calls remain backward compatible and server-side authorization remains authoritative; only discovery becomes phase-focused, with a documented explicit raw-tool opt-in.

questions.question: What should one project gate verify?
questions.assumed: Backend and frontend suites, feature wiring, deterministic agent-accuracy checks, and environment-aware browser/Blender probes that distinguish unavailable prerequisites from actual failures.

questions.question: What evidence is required before declaring the mission complete?
questions.assumed: All unit and integration suites pass; real runtime file journeys succeed; rendered collision checks pass at supported widths; connection states are truthful; the MCP catalogue and instructions pass focused accuracy evaluations; and the restored gate is green.
